learningObjective: Reason about intra-warp branch divergence: serialization cost, uniform-branch immunity, predication trade-off.

canonicalClaims.claim: Intra-warp branch divergence serializes the warp across the divergent paths; branches whose condition is uniform across all lanes in a warp do not diverge; predication (via `?:` or select) avoids divergence but may execute both arms.
conditions: SIMT execution model; standard nvcc code generation.
nonImplications: Does not imply divergence always halves throughput.
Does not imply Volta+ ITS eliminates divergence cost.

misconceptions.claim: All conditional constructs compile to divergent branches.
Uniform (per-warp uniform) branches are always as expensive as divergent branches.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Uniform branches have no divergence cost.

misconceptions.claim: Predication is always faster than divergent branches.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Predication computes both arms; expensive arms make branches preferable when uniform.

misconceptions.claim: Volta+ Independent Thread Scheduling eliminates divergence cost.
misconceptions.whyWrong: ITS enables independent forward progress; per-warp issue and serialization of divergent paths remain.

implementationFacts: Per-warp active mask tracks which lanes execute each path.
`selp.f32` and predicated `mov`/`fma` are common predication ops.
